## Today: you build, I help 🛠️

No lecture. Both blocks are **your project time**.

- I am in the main room the whole time 🎧
- Breakout rooms for focused work
- ✋ any time you want me to look at something

::: notes
0–5 min. Keep it short — every minute of talking is a minute they are not coding.
:::

## Feedback on your proposals 💬 {.smaller}

⏱️ 10 min

Three things I saw in your `PROJECT.md` files:

1. [most common strength] 🌟
2. [most common risk — usually: too ambitious] ⚠️
3. [most common gap — usually: no real input file] 📄

. . .

If your scope feels big: cut it in half. Then cut it again. ✂️

::: notes
5–15 min. Fill these in after reading their proposals. Concrete, anonymous, kind.
:::

## How to start when you are stuck 🧗 {.smaller}

1. Write the **steps in comments** first 📝
2. Make the smallest version run — even printing "hello" from your tool
3. One function at a time, test it, commit it 💾
4. `print()` everything while you work 👀

. . .

> Working and ugly beats elegant and unfinished. Always. 🌱

::: notes
15–25 min. This is the only "teaching" today. Then get out of the way.
:::

## Today's goal 🎯 {.smaller}

By the end of the second block:

- ✅ Your repo has a `PROJECT.md` and a script that **runs**
- ✅ It reads your input file — even if it only prints the first line
- ✅ At least one function written and committed

. . .

That is a real milestone. The rest is iteration 🔁

::: notes
25–30 min. A concrete finish line prevents the "I'll start at home" drift.
:::

## Work time 🛠️ {.smaller}

⏱️ Rest of the block

**How to get help**

- ✋ Raise your hand — I will join your room
- 💬 Chat for quick questions
- 👥 Room 1 = "quiet focus", Room 2 = "talk while working"

. . .

**Before you leave: commit and push.** 💾

::: notes
30–80 min. Visit rooms in rotation. Keep a list of who you have checked on — online it is easy to miss the quiet ones.
Note recurring problems to address in block 2.
:::
